identity.title: Improved Regret Bounds for Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound in Bayesian Optimization

problem.claim: Bayesian optimization with a function drawn from a known Gaussian process seeks to minimize cumulative regret.

gap.claim: The authors state that existing GP-UCB regret bounds leave a gap relative to the best upper bound provided by Scarlett (2018).

contributions.claim: Derives a high-probability \tilde{O}(\sqrt{T}) cumulative-regret bound for GP-UCB under a Matérn kernel with some smoothness.
Derives an O(\sqrt{T \ln^2 T}) regret bound under a squared exponential kernel.
Uses concentration behavior of the GP-UCB-realized input sequence to refine the treatment of GP information gain.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present their bounds as filling the gap between existing GP-UCB upper bounds and Scarlett’s (2018) best upper bound.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GP-UCB achieves \tilde{O}(\sqrt{T}) cumulative regret with high probability under a Matérn kernel with some smoothness.
The authors report an O(\sqrt{T \ln^2 T}) regret bound under a squared exponential kernel.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames Bayesian optimization as minimizing regret for a function drawn from a known GP.
States a high-probability \tilde{O}(\sqrt{T}) GP-UCB regret bound for a suitably smooth Matérn kernel.
States an O(\sqrt{T \ln^2 T}) bound for the squared exponential kernel.
Characterizes the results as closing a gap with Scarlett’s (2018) best upper bound.
Attributes the improvement to concentration analysis of the input sequence generated by GP-UCB and refined information-gain control.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the improved regret bounds to a specific proof mechanism: analyzing concentration of the algorithm-generated input sequence to refine information-gain handling.

lessons.interpretation: A paper can make a theoretical advance easier to assess by connecting each headline bound to the analytical bottleneck and the mechanism that addresses it.
lessons.application: When presenting a new bound, explicitly identify the quantity or dependency that prior analyses handled coarsely and state how the proof changes its control.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the contribution is primarily empirical or when the abstract cannot identify a concrete mechanism.

unknowns: The exact Matérn smoothness condition, hidden factors in \tilde{O}, confidence dependence, horizon conventions, and quantitative comparison with prior bounds are not specified.
The abstract does not provide proof details or independently verifiable evidence beyond the authors’ stated theoretical results.
